profile.headline: Software Engineer | U.S. Marine Corps Veteran
profile.geoLocationName: San Diego County, California, United States
profile.summary:
In the U.S. Marine Corps, I specialized in logistics, working as a Motor Transport Operator and later leading a team of 5 Marines as a Corporal.

Having earned a degree in Computer Science, I've shifted into a software engineering career. I'm focused on creating practical software solutions that enhance daily life, streamline workflows, and create net positive good in what I build and contribute to. I consistently seek to expand my technical knowledge, prioritizing growth over adherence to specific tech stacks or languages.

My professional experience spans mid-level roles to small team management. I've handled various projects and feature requests, consistently finding inventive solutions to optimize workflow and enhance productivity.

Currently, I'm actively seeking full-time opportunities, aiming to leverage my skills and technical proficiency to make a meaningful impact in the Software Engineering field, benefiting both end-users and the company.

For potential job opportunities, you can contact me at jason.j.lee4@gmail.com or connect on LinkedIn.

Technical expertise includes PHP, Laravel, TypeScript, Javascript, React, RESTful APIs, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, Cypress, MySQL, GitHub, DataDog, Sentry, Redis, Docker, MobX, Circle CI, Jenkins, Argo, Amplitude, Kustomer, Python, Java, C#, AWS, C++, C, Visual Studio, Atlassian Suite (Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket).

positions.description: Skills: C++ · Software Design · React.js · Node.js · Figma (Software)

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Promoted from Junior Software Engineer to Mid-level Software Engineer in 2023.

Spearheaded shipment label purchasing strategy with PHP/Laravel v8 by leveraging Action classes and recurring cron jobs, leading to cost savings exceeding $215K for the operations team.

Implemented automated bulk re-prescription system with Laravel QueryBuilder, Action classes, and React v18, reducing manual re-prescription efforts to a streamlined two-click process and saving providers 10 hours per week.

Automated providers’ manual outreach workflow with PHP, SQL, and Tableau, resulting in a 20% reduction in medical providers' redundancies, translating to over $700 in daily savings and optimizing provider productivity.

Integrated UPS as a second shipment carrier with RESTful APIs and Redis rate limiting to increase shipping flexibility, saving $350-400K annually in label costs.

Developed event and data-model-driven webhooks with RESTful APIs for seamless migration and synchronization of subscription discount data with Recharge service during discount code applications.

Refactored production codebase to modular monolith and laid groundwork for a microservice architecture by implementing independent components utilizing Data Transfer Objects and Contracts, thus ensuring robust domain boundaries.

Orchestrated robust end-to-end testing with Cypress and PHPUnit; resolved bugs, created monitors and dashboards with Sentry, DataDog, and Amplitude to track errors, system performance, and uptime.

Partnered cross-functionally with product managers, designers, and marketing to devise solutions for complex challenges, driving successful product launches and user adoption.

positions.description:
Promoted from Software Engineer I to Software Engineer II within the first 9 months.

Designed and deployed automation tests with Python and VMWare for real-time components simulating unmanned aircrafts, creating a 30% decline in manual testing hours and ensuring precision in testing outcomes.

Developed scripts in Python and TestComplete to link automation tests to specific requirements, eliminating manually tracking thousands of software requirements and saving engineer work time.

positions.title: Treasurer and Graphics Artist for Orange Coast College Veterans Association
positions.description:
● Appointed to Treasurer on January 2017

● Responsible for maintaining accurate record-keeping of club finances, seek additional opportunities to raise budget to increase efficacy in club spending for promotions, events, and volunteering efforts.

● Commissioned by OCCVA club President Joe Perez-Marchese to design a new logo to be printed on shirts, banners, promotions, and distributions related to the club. Commission accepted and approved in December 2016; completed on January 2017.

positions.title: Math Tutor
positions.description:
● Assisted students in mathematics ranging from beginner algebra to Calculus 1.

● Active as core staff member of on-campus veteran-to-veteran tutoring program to provide student veterans with assistance in mathematics. This program began during Fall 2016: the principle behind this initiative was to have a steady veteran presence at the Veterans Resource Center on-campus to be available to all student veterans. I am also responsible for promoting the use of the Student Success Center itself for additional tutors on a variety of school subjects.

●Focused on using visual and auditory learning styles, using dry erase materials and multiple approaches to explaining the same mathematical concepts when one method does not work for students. Flexible and patient in aiding students to solve problems without shortcuts or memorization, as patience is key to bridging the gap between a student and his/her light bulb moment.

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description:
● Learned Python within the first week of the internship; began developing by second week to address real-world problems that the System Engineers of the Systems Engineering, Integration, and Testing (SEIT) team were facing.

● Utilized Python to create scripts for automating redundant tasks in validating and generating meaningful data from hexadecimal codes used by the NATO Air-Ground Surveillance vehicle. Parsed and converted hexadecimal code against hundreds of tables and spreadsheets to generate human readable information, saving engineers two weeks' worth of work hours during critical drone flight testing periods.

● Created scripts to generate and validate the information in Integrated Design Documents for System Engineers, saving both time and money for future editions while minimizing the need for engineers to manually write and visually validate the information and tables in the IDD.

● Utilized data structures such as dictionaries, lists, AND/OR/XOR bit manipulation, along with essential loops and input/output relevant to all object-oriented programming.

● End of Internship: August 18, 2017

positions.title: Corporal
positions.description:
● Supervised 5 Marines with performing logistics and accountability for field operations with over 40 military vehicles. My duties involved ensuring the Marines under my care were properly licensed, maintain and improve their capabilities in operating our military equipment. I was also responsible for the welfare, accountability, and discipline of the Marines under my care; this meant that I was accountable for ensuring my peers were fairly given opportunities to succeed in their job specialty, ensure they showed up to work on time, complete their assigned tasks, and even something as simple as being the mentor to check on their mental and physical health or make sure they had food to eat.

● Received 6 awards, 2 of which are for exceptional leadership, initiative, and performance of duties within and outside of immediate occupational specialty. Received first commendation for volunteering at a high school to demonstrate knowledge and proficiency of the HMMWV ("humvee") vehicle used in service to technical metal shop class; received second commendation for proactively assisting in artillery duties during 2-week Summer field training exercise in 29 Palms, CA.

projects.title: OCC Veterans Resource Center - Electronic Login System
projects.description:
The on-campus Veterans Resource Center at Orange Coast College has traditionally used a paper-and-pen sign in system, where the student veteran who wishes to use the lounge and its computers must sign in with their name, date, branch of service, and time. The sheets collected are shelved and stored for demonstrating the frequency in which the lounge is used by student veterans, with the possibility of using the collected data to strengthen justification for further funding in the future. This project will rid of this by-hand sign-in process by using electronic means to make an already simple method even simpler.

My project partner, Gene Strickland, and I have built a working prototype using C++ and Visual Studio 2015: the system revolves around using I/O file streams and string streams to check user's input against what is stored in a text file, and if the input matches the data in said text file a time stamp is recorded into another text file with the time, day, month, year, and the student veteran's name, student ID, and branch of service. 

In simpler terms, a student veteran logging into the resource center will input his/her student ID into the program. If this student had not registered prior, the system will inquire if the user had registered before; if he/she had in fact registered before, the system will prompt the user to input the student ID again (which assumes that the user’s input had a typo or was not an 8-digit identification number); if he/she hadn’t registered at all, then the user will be prompted to register a full name, student ID, and branch of service to store into a user registry text file that serves as a small scale database. Once registered, the student veteran can input his/her student ID to login.

====================================================================================
Updates/improvements to come:
- Add more documentation to functions utilized in the program
- Improve efficiency of class functions to reduce redundancy
